notes: Step [3] now passes --window $session_date..$session_date, correct for the designed one-session-per-morning cadence. But window.from is the START of the KRX witness fetch (fetch_state.rs seeds krx_cursor from window.from, runs to krx_through), so if a morning is MISSED the gap spans 2+ sessions and only the latest day gets a witness — intermediate days stay Unknown while the bounded ingest tries to advance across them. Fix direction: derive window.from from the daily watermark in the ingest checkpoint (the script already reads it for count_advanced/SYMS) instead of the session date. title: session-morning.sh step [7] pace check KILLS the ingest on a catch-up run, leaving a PARTIAL catalog
notes: The in-ingest pace check polls every 30s and kills ls-ingest as soon as it projects past LS_SM_INGEST_BY (default 09:05), then exits 40. That is right for the attended path it was built for — a universe landing after 09:10 is useless because head v34 builds its opening range only from 09:00-15:00 live bars. It is WRONG for a catch-up run, where the mount is already conceded and the whole point is to advance the catalog: the kill leaves a partial watermark distribution, i.e. exactly the half-finished state the catch-up exists to prevent. Nothing in the script distinguishes the two callers. Workaround used on 2026-07-31: LS_SM_INGEST_BY=09:40 with LS_SM_UNIVERSE_BY left at 09:10, so the ingest completes and the clean stand-down happens at the step [8] gate instead. Fix direction: an explicit catch-up mode (or --no-pace-gate) that skips the step [7] kill while keeping the step [8] universe refusal.

title: Wire `make script-check` into `make gate-run` so a reworded probe literal is PREEMPTED, not merely diagnosable
notes: PR #260 follow-up (a), highest operational value of the four. Today nothing runs script-check automatically, so a reworded probe literal in BIN_PROBE_LITERALS reaches the 08:45 chain as a hard exit 64: diagnosable at the moment it costs the most clock, never preempted. R10's registry-drift assertion is what bounds this. MECHANICS: scripts/gate-run.sh AND scripts/gate-run-check.sh must move in ONE commit -- gate-run-check.sh asserts the exact step list, so editing gate-run.sh alone reds the gate. PREREQUISITE, do not skip: script-check carries a KNOWN FLAKE ('normal mode: the stalled ingest is killed', ~1 run in 4-6 under load; the step [7] poll races the stub's own 10s sleep). It predates the freshness work (reproduced at 92ba1ed) and fixing the pace gate was an explicit non-goal of the #260 plan. Wiring it in as-is imports that flake rate into the commit gate, which is how a gate stops being believed. Either fix/quarantine that one assertion first or land it alongside. Runtime of the target is seconds (stubs, offline, no gateway), so cost is not the objection.

title: Replay calendar-refresh against its REAL binary in the script-check harness (the #258-guard carrier is the least-covered binary)
notes: PR #260 follow-up (b). calendar-refresh carries PR #258's forward-horizon guard yet is structurally the least-covered binary in the harness: the argv replay covers only calendar-fetch-inputs, and every freshness axis runs against STUBS. So nothing today asserts the registered probe literal is present in a REAL compiled artifact -- R10 checks the Rust SOURCES, and the fixture PLANTS the literal into its stub. That is the exact shape the source doc warns about: a guard's verdict certifies neither its own presence nor its inputs. Model the work on the existing calendar-fetch-inputs replay: marshal the step [4] argv, strip credentials, run it against target/debug/calendar-refresh so the check cannot drift from the parser it guards, and assert the literal via 'grep -qa' (presence, not the count form -- KTD4). Requires the real binary present; report loudly if absent, as the existing replay does.

title: Register probe literals for the other six preflight binaries -- cost it at ~4.1s per large-binary MISS, not 0.18s
notes: PR #260 follow-up (c). The content axis is registered for 1 of 7 binaries, so an overridden run (LS_SM_ALLOW_STALE_BINARIES=1 waives the mtime axis) leaves six binaries with NO freshness evidence at all; the preflight banner says so. The registry is SPARSE BY DESIGN (R5) and grows when a guard ships, not on a schedule -- registering an arbitrary literal for a binary with no recent load-bearing change asserts nothing. COST, corrected: the original KTD4 figure of 0.18s worst case was measured at an interactive prompt where grep is aliased to ugrep; the script resolves /usr/bin/grep (BSD), where an ABSENT literal on the 262 MB ls-ingest costs ~4.1s -- 23x higher. A miss is a full scan, and a miss is exactly what refuses. Registering the three LARGE binaries therefore puts roughly 12s on the 08:45 path, not ~0.5s. Budget that against the 09:05 ingest deadline before registering. The registered 4.8 MB calendar-refresh costs 0.05s, so today's cost is nil. Registry separator is '|', so a literal containing one is silently truncated on both sides -- the structural field-count check in script-check covers that.

notes: Supersedes rung1-ladder-reentry-net-positive-head (sample-sufficiency turn, plan 2026-08-05-001; TURN-LOG 2026-08-06). WHY THE CONDITION MOVED: the old unblock 'net RoR > 0 with the armed cost model' is satisfiable by LUCK — on the v35 sample the session-block bootstrap puts the share of null replicates above zero at 0.4955, so a coin-flip head meets it about half the time. NEW UNBLOCK: the candidate clears the frozen margin in lab/config/sample-margin.json — net RoR > E[max of 29 null trials] + z(95%) x SE(candidate), the False Strategy Theorem at the frozen trial count and cross-trial dispersion. HOW TO CHECK, from adapters/nautilus (the lab crate is skipped from the repo root): LS_DATA_HOME=<home> LS_REPORT_RUN=<run> cargo run -q -p nautilus-ls-lab --bin lab-research -- report sample (or ./target/debug/lab-research report sample once built). Its 'MARGIN VERDICT' line is the gate — but read the line after it too: 'RE-DERIVATION REQUIRED' means the candidate's catalog fingerprint differs from the frozen one, so the margin does NOT bind until it is re-derived, whatever the verdict line says. The verb exits 0 for every verdict, so the exit code is not the gate. v35 is REFUSED (net RoR -0.000607 vs threshold +0.224823 at SE 0.087002). DO NOT EXPECT A LEVER SEARCH TO GET THERE: the head's gross edge sits ~9x below this sample's detection floor; ~8,600 closed trades (~3,499 CALENDAR sessions, ~14 years) are needed against 54 covered — see queue orb-sample-acquisition-decision. Once a head DOES clear: this is still a code-hash move (code_change_resets_to_rung_1), so re-entry STARTS with a fresh prereg re-registration (v3+) — bands re-derived from that head's closed-trade distribution via the Protective formula, reproduced in lab/tests/prereg_derivation.rs, and RUNG1-PREFLIGHT.md step-3 literals moved in the same commit — all before any genesis dispatch. title: Decide the ORB sample acquisition — a fresh catalog at a wider lookback, or stand the arc down
notes: Successor staged by the sample-sufficiency turn (plan 2026-08-05-001; TURN-LOG 2026-08-06), so the STAND-DOWN verdict does not terminate without a next step. THE VERDICT: at the pinned target (the measured gross per-trade edge +0.028422 R, 95% confidence, 80% power, design effect 2.1579) the head needs ~8,629 closed trades. At the observed 2.4667 closed trades per CALENDAR session (111 trades over the 45 sessions the run's range covers — NOT the 4.625 per trade-producing session, which is the clustering unit and a different denominator) that is ~3,499 KST sessions, about 14 years, against 54 sessions of catalog coverage. SHORTFALL ~3,445 sessions. NO ROW OF THE TARGET-EFFECT BAND IS REACHABLE: even the design-effect-corrected upper end (+0.204 R) needs 68 sessions against 54. RE-EVALUATE THIS VERDICT WHEN, and only when, one of: (a) the catalog covers materially more sessions; (b) a credibly larger target effect is measured — the band, not the point, is what a re-read should move; (c) the clustering falls (ICC 0.327 at cluster size 4.54 is what costs the factor of 2.16); or (d) the head starts trading a larger share of the sessions it sees, which raises the calendar rate directly. Re-read from adapters/nautilus with: LS_DATA_HOME=<home> LS_REPORT_RUN=<run> cargo run -q -p nautilus-ls-lab --bin lab-research -- report sample. THE ACQUISITION IS ITS OWN DECISION, NOT A CHORE: it is a FRESH CATALOG at a wider lookback, not an incremental extension — accumulate never fetches below the watermark — so it is budget-bound (a multi-year multi-symbol daily+minute pull against the LS gateway's IGW00201 cumulative budget) and it MOVES the catalog fingerprint, the universe hash and the data range. That re-baselines every prior measurement, including this turn's own margin provenance, which then has to be re-derived before it binds. Prefer HISTORY over breadth: added sessions raise effective n roughly in proportion, added breadth adds trades inside blocks already held, and max_concurrent 7 caps how much breadth converts at all. Standing the ORB arc down is a legitimate arm of this decision. Do NOT spend a lever turn before this is settled — at effective n 51 nothing is attributable to anything.

title: Make report sample's supply probe read catalog METADATA, not every bar — it decodes the whole catalog to count daily dates
notes: Deferred from the sample-sufficiency turn's own code review (plan 2026-08-05-001; TURN-LOG 2026-08-06). WHAT: report_sample's supply probe calls nautilus_ls::ingest::read_all_bars, which materializes EVERY bar in the catalog — minute and daily, all OHLCV columns — and then keeps only the distinct KST dates of the daily ones. Measured ~12s on the current 69 MB / 5,129-file catalog, where the read dominates the verb's runtime. WHY IT MATTERS NOW: this turn's whole recommendation is growing the catalog from 54 to ~3,499 sessions (~65x). Row-decoding cost scales with total volume, so the verb an operator is meant to re-run whenever checking sample sufficiency would become a multi-minute wait at exactly the scale it recommends reaching. read_all_bars's own doc comment already warns it 'must not be used per symbol' for this reason. LEAD: the vendored nautilus-persistence ParquetDataCatalog exposes get_intervals / get_directory_intervals, which derive per-file timestamp ranges from filenames via parse_filename_timestamps without decoding any parquet rows — confirm daily-bar file granularity is per-session-range before relying on it, and consider filtering the bars directory to Day-aggregation identifiers instead. NOT A BLOCKER: the current read is correct, just costly; report_tiers sets the same full-read precedent, so fixing one is an opportunity to fix both. Two reviewers (performance + the cross-model adversarial pass) raised it independently.

title: Measure PAIRED per-session power from the seven surviving off-flip arms — offline, gates the ORB stand-down
notes: Arm E of orb-sample-acquisition-decision (plan 2026-08-07-001), selected by the operator 2026-08-07. THAT ITEM STAYS OPEN until this returns — this measurement is what decides it. WHY IT EXISTS: the sample-sufficiency verdict measures ABSOLUTE detectability (is the head's edge distinguishable from zero — no, by ~9x). Every lever turn asks a DIFFERENT question: does armed beat off-flip over the SAME sessions. That is a paired comparison with its own standard error, and nothing in the tree has measured it. So TURN-LOG's 'at this effective sample size nothing is attributable to anything' is established for absolute attribution and UNTESTED for paired attribution. This is a hypothesis, not a correction of that verdict. FEASIBLE OFFLINE, VERIFIED 2026-08-07: the seven off-flip arms survive as run artifacts in data/turn4-cost-scratch/runs/ (20260731T023106Z-backtest-orb-v91 .. 20260731T023324Z-backtest-orb-v97), each with performance.json carrying 113 trade records with realized_r, risk_capital and ts_closed, on the SAME catalog_fingerprint ac026541 and the SAME strategy_code_hash 7571abef as v35. No backtest re-run needed, no gateway, no ingest. FRAGILITY: data/ is gitignored, so those artifacts are machine-local — if lost, the seven arms must be re-run before this can proceed. WHAT TO MEASURE: per-KST-session paired delta between v35 and each off-flip arm, its SE and CI, then whether each recorded off-flip delta (0.0237 to 0.0811 net RoR, TURN-LOG 2026-07-31 table) is attributable at the 24 sessions held. OPEN CHOICE (Q4 of the plan): pair on net RoR or on mean per-trade r — the first matches the objective the levers were judged on, the second is less sensitive to session-level risk-capital swings; decide against the artifact and record the choice with the result. VERDICT ROUTING: if paired power is adequate, the ORB arc is NOT sample-blocked for lever work and the stand-down recommendation is withdrawn pending a re-read; if it is not, the stand-down closes on measurement rather than on a calculation about a different question. CONSTRAINTS: offline only, no strategy code, no governed param — strategy_code_hash and config/preregistration.json must both be unchanged at the end, verified not assumed.

title: TR-parameterized minute-depth probe — the capability arm D needs to be priced at all
notes: Successor staged by the sample-acquisition close (TURN-LOG 2026-08-10; plan 2026-08-07-002), so arm D does not terminate unasked. WHAT: LS_INGEST_MODE=probe-lookback is bound to the t8412 fetcher (domestic KRX equity N-minute) and LS_INGEST_LANE_FILE selects CREDENTIALS, NOT AN INSTRUMENT — pointing it at another lane sends the same domestic request under a different token and answers nothing. The missing piece is the backward window walk (probe_minute_lookback, 7-day windows, break-on-empty) parameterized by TR / instrument domain, writing its own per-lane minute-lookback.json. NOT AN SDK EXPANSION: t8465 (KOSPI200 futures/options N-min), o3103 (overseas futures min), t8418 (sector index N-min) are already support.implemented with live-smoke targets and lane files on disk. SPEND CONDITION — build this only when one holds: (a) a coarse raw-probe reading on t8465 or o3103 shows materially deeper served history than the domestic ~359-day rolling window, which is the only thing that would make a pivot change the sample answer; or (b) an ORB-shaped arc is re-opened on a non-domestic instrument for a reason other than supply. A coarse deeper-or-not signal needs NO harness: make raw-probe accepts an arbitrary TR/path/body and prints body_len, so a single request at a deep start date separates 'much deeper' from 'same rolling window'. Only an EXACT floor needs the walk. INHERITED TRAP: the anchor is wall-clock-derived inside run_probe (last_closed_session, 16:30 KST buffer) and gated on the calendar's proven-session frontier — select_recent_session returns None at the first Unknown it walks into, so any generalized probe inherits the same day-of-week coupling unless it also parameterizes the anchor.
